THIS CRL.P IS FILED U/S 482 CR.PC (FILED U/S 528 BNSS) PRAYING TO QUASH THE ORDER OF COGNIZANCE DATED 30/08/2024 PASSED BY THE XXIV ADDITIONAL CHIEF JUDICIAL MAGISTRATE, AT BENGALURU IN CC.NO.20311/2024 REGISTERED BY THE WEST WOMEN POLICE STATION,
BENGALURU CITY, FOR OFFENCES PUNISHABLE UNDER SECTIONS 494, 498 A, 417 OF THE INDIAN PENAL CODE.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM :
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MOHAMMAD NAWAZ  ORAL ORDER
The proceedings in CC No.20311/2024 pending on the file of the Court of XXIV Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate at Bengaluru are sought to be quashed in this petition.

entities.text: Court of XXIV Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate at Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Chargesheet is filed against the petitioner for the offence punishable under Section 494, 498A and 417 of IPC.
The proceedings are initiated by the respondent No.2 herein.
3. An application is filed under Section 359(8) r/w Section 528 of the BNSS, 2023 to permit the parties to NC: 2025:KHC:51259 HC-KAR compound the offence and on that basis to quash the proceedings.
4. Application is accompanied with the joint affidavit of petitioner and respondent No.2.

It is stated that the petitioner and respondent No.2/defacto complainant have settled the matter before the I Additional Family Judge, Bengaluru in M.C.No.7565/2025.
5.

The dispute arises out of a matrimonial dicord, wherein the petitioner and respondent No.2,
present before the Court would confirm the settlement taken place between them.

Respondent No.2 Maheshwaraiah D vs State Of Karnataka on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4079702/
2 as per the joint affidavit, has agreed to withdraw all proceedings arising out of the said dispute.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Narinder Singh and Others V. State of Punjab and Another reported in (2014) 6 SCC 466 has held that when the parties have reached the settlement and on that basis,
petition for quashing the criminal proceedings is filed, the guiding NC: 2025:KHC:51259 HC-KAR factor in such cases would be:(i) to secure the ends of justice; or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court.

entities.text: Narinder Singh and Others V. State of Punjab and Another reported in (2014) 6 SCC 466
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further held that the criminal cases having overwhelmingly and predominantly civil character, particularly those arising out of commercial transactions or arising out of matrimonial relationship or family disputes should be quashed when the parties have resolved their entire disputes among themselves.

7. In B.S.Joshi and others V. State of Haryana and another reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has upheld the powers of the High Court under Section 482 of the code to quash criminal proceedings, where dispute is of a private nature and the compromise is entered into between the parties.

entities.text: B.S.Joshi and others V. State of Haryana and another reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. In the facts and circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that the interest of justice will be met if the proceedings now pending against the petitioner are quashed.

Accordingly the following:
NC: 2025:KHC:51259 HC-KAR ORDER Petition is allowed.
The entire proceedings in CC No.20311/2024 pending on the file of the Court of XXIV Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate at Bengaluru are quashed.
